{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Flatbread|Flatbread]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]]

'''Batooru''' is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|North Indian]] [[Cookbook:Fermentation|fermented]] bread similar to [[Cookbook:Fried Wheat Bread Balls (Bhatoora)|bhatoora]], but is mostly popular in traditional Himachali cuisine. This bread requires overnight preparation.

==Ingredients==

* [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|Wheat flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tsp [[Cookbook:Ghee|ghee]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]]

==Procedure==

# Mix wheat flour and salt together. Add ghee and mix well so that there are no lumps and the ghee is evenly absorbed. 
# Add water in small amounts and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] well until the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] becomes soft and pliable. 
# When the dough is ready, form the dough into balls and roll them flat. Keep it slightly thick, unlike a bhatoora which is rolled to be very thin. Place the rolled batooru on a clean cloth and cover them with another moist cloth. Leave them covered overnight.
# The next morning, take the batooru out from cloth and shallow [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] them like a parantha.
# Serve them hot, especially with with sabzi (spicy cooked vegetables), [[Cookbook:Lassi|lassi]], and [[Cookbook:Mango Chutney|mango pickles]].
